extracted.intended_audience: press officers, PR practitioners, and communications professionals preparing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and distributing press releases to maximize media pickup, based on Davis's empirical findings about resource asymmetry and source–journalist networks. Emphasizes tailoring, distribution mode, spokesperson availability, allied sources, and pre-emptive framing to substitute for lacking network position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target-media-fit
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should be optimized for a specific paper or wire (not blasted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Davis documents corporate PR successes by tailoring distinct releases for different outlets (e.g., Financial Times vs The Sun vs trade titles). Craft releases to match the target outlet's audience, tone, and editorial priors rather than sending identical copy to a broad list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat-relationship leverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup is dramatically amplified by long-cultivated journalist contacts; pickup-rate is a function of the issuer's historical reliability on the beat, not just the current text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained reliability and trust on a journalist's beat matter more than a single well-written release. If you have established beat relationships, routine announcements convert at higher rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode-of-distribution (City-page / financial-press bypass)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mode-of-distribution can be as important as content: a brief embargoed pre-release to City editors converts at far higher rates than an open wire blast for corporate releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted embargoes or tailored pre-release communications to specific desks (e.g., City or financial editors) rather than broad wires when seeking higher conversion in specialized press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure-group asymmetry / tactics for resource-poor issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource-poor groups achieve pickup only when they piggyback on corporate releases (counter-quote), break exclusives, or deliver pre-packaged investigation material; pure announcement-style releases from resource-poor sources have near-zero pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack institutional resources, rely on strategies that substitute credibility or novelty: attach to larger actors' stories, offer exclusives, or provide ready-to-use investigative material and evidence rather than simple announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-reframing (trade-union case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases reach lay press only when framed to match the receiving audience's editorial priors (e.g., unions' releases succeed when framed as consumer-impact stories rather than labor-relations stories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reframe issues in terms that matter to the target outlet's readers (consumer impact, scandal, local effect), not in the source's default policy or organizational frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson availability premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup increases sharply when a named spokesperson is on standby for an immediate phone call from any inquiring journalist within ~30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a named, easily reachable contact and ensure they are prepared to respond quickly. Journalists are more likely to use a story when they can get an on-the-record comment fast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-source mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple separate trusted sources echo a release talking-point, downstream pickup multiplies; releases that name allied parties willing to be contacted have higher conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and arrange availability of allied spokespeople or independent corroborating sources who can be contacted to confirm or expand on the story, increasing perceived credibility and uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-emption of routine criticisms
rubrics_metrics.description: A release that includes the obvious critic's likely objection plus a substantive response converts more reliably than one that leaves the critic uncalled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate predictable counter-arguments and provide responses, evidence, or context within the release so journalists do not have to pause to chase rebuttal quotes or caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute for network position (pickup-worthiness implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup is determined more by the issuer's structural position in the source–journalist network than by release text quality; operational implication is to instrument the release with everything required to substitute for that network position when it is absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you lack a strong network position, explicitly build credibility into the release: named expert quotes, immediate spokesperson contact, pre-emptive critic responses, allied sources willing to be contacted, exclusives or embargoed outreach, and pre-packaged materials. The aim is to emulate the trust and resource advantages that well-positioned issuers enjoy.
